title: STUDY TOPIC JESUS AND THE SPIRIT. Part 5
devotional:
The Spirit at the conception of Jesus.

We all know and love the Christmas story, we are familiar with the main characters, Mary, Joseph, angels, wise men, shepherds, and Herod. However there is one character in the nativity we either completely ignore or give very little thought to, and that is the person of the Holy Spirit. The nativity story is recorded both in Matthew and Luke, and if you were to compare them you will notice that they are very different. The reason for this is because each writer is telling the same story but from a different perspective. Matthew is telling the Story from Joseph’s perspective, while Luke is telling it from Mary’s perspective. However despite the difference in perspective and content they are both in agreement about the role of Holy Spirit in the conception. They both record that an angelic being told Mary that she would conceive by the power of the Holy Spirit.

Luke tells us that Gabriel spoke to Mary. ‘Mary asked the angel, “But how can this happen? I am a virgin.”The angel replied, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. So the baby to be born will be holy, and he will be called the Son of God.’ 1:34-35.

Matthew tells us that the angel of the Lord spoke to Joseph. ‘As he considered this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream. “Joseph, son of David,” the angel said, “do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife. For the child within her was conceived by the Holy Spirit.’ Matthew 1:20

I think we need to consider the significance of this. The same message about the role of the Holy Spirit is delivered twice by an angelic being to two different people at two different times.

There may be a number of reasons why we are not too inclined to consider the role of the Holy Spirit in the birth narrative of Jesus.

1. We find it easier to relate to the human characters of the story.

We are familiar with Mary and Joseph, we know their backstory, we know that she is probably a young teenager who scandalously conceived outside the legitimate confines of marriage. We know that because Joseph was a righteous man he was unsure as to what he should do. Should he divorce her? Divorce being the only way of nullifying the betrothal covenant.

This is a drama, a story that catches our imagination and pulls on our emotions. We are slow to recognise that the Holy Spirit is there working in the background, making things happen, we might consider him playing a vital role, but we would not see him as one of the main characters.

2.Maybe the uniqueness of this event causes us to overlook the role of the Spirit in this situation.

We all know that there will never be an other miraculous conception. What the Holy Spirit did in the life of Mary was an abnormal one off event. However, although the work of the Spirit in Mary was unique and unrepeated, the character of the Holy Spirit, the principles by which he works and goals or objectives he has [to produce in us the reality of Jesus,] are the same. Our lives need to become an echo of the nativity, where Jesus is formed in us and revealed through us. Let’s be honest we would rather watch the nativity as a sanitised children’s play than be part of it, however, we all need our own personalised ‘nativity’ story... Our lives need to become an echo of the original nativity.

3. A third possible reason why we ignore the role of the Holy Spirit in the nativity is that we may assume that Mary’s and Joseph's understanding of who the Holy Spirit is the same or similar to our understanding of the Spirit. So when we read ‘The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you,’ we must not assume that Mary understood it as we do.

We need to keep in mind that Mary and Joseph lived at a time when Rabbinical teaching was prevalent.

‘For centuries according to many of the rabbis, those teachers who most influenced the thinking of the first century Palestinian Judaism, the Spirit had been silent, his work was over and his activity was a past phenomenon. The Spirit had indeed given Israel the Torah, lots prophets and the whole of its scriptures, but having done that, his work had ceased.’ Gerald Hawthorne.

It was a common belief that the Holy Spirit had departed from Israel so when the angel declared that Mary would conceive by the power of the Holy Spirit, he was telling Mary that her experience of God would be outside her understanding. Sometimes God will do things in our lives that may appear to be outside the normal or the usual. Sadly this fact can lead to people doing things that are either ridiculous, selfish, dangerous our immoral suggesting that the Holy Spirit told them to. However, the Holy Spirit is called the Holy Spirit, and he will never ask anyone to act outside the moral will of God. He will never resort to sin, deceit or abusive manipulation to accomplish the will of the father in your life or the lives of others. There was absolutely no immorality in Mary’s conception outside of marriage.
prayer: Father, thank you that the work of the Spirit may be unusual, but will never be immoral or egotistical.
